question.worked_solution:
If $X∼\text{Geom}(p),$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}(1-p)^{x-1}p, & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.7),$ so the distribution of $X$ in this case is

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}(0.3)^{x-1}(0.7), & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

There are infinitely many values of $X$ such that $X>5.$ However, we can simplify the computation by using the complement instead:

$$
P(X>5)=1-P(X\le 5)
$$

Computing the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 5) & =P(X\in \{1,2,3,4,5\}) \\  & =P(X=1)+P(X=2)+P(X=3)+P(X=4)+P(X=5) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4)+f(5) \\  & =(0.3)^{0}(0.7)+(0.3)^{1}(0.7)+(0.3)^{2}(0.7)+(0.3)^{3}(0.7)+(0.3)^{4}(0.7) \\  & =0.99757.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>5) & =1-P(X\le 5) \\  & =1-0.99757 \\  & ≈0.0024.\end{aligned}
$$
